quotes.quote: Optional participant that can assist vendors and finders in handling and disclosing vulnerability information.
Vendor that provides a product or technology to a downstream vendor.
All parties should clearly and securely communicate and negotiate expectations and timelines.
Finder should provide clear documentation and artifacts to support vulnerability verification.
Vendors should be aware that publication of fixes can disclose the presence of the same vulnerability in other vendors’ components.
To reduce confusion when multiple coordinators are involved, one coordinator should be selected as lead.
within 24 hours of the manufacturer becoming aware of it
within 72 hours of the manufacturer becoming aware of the actively exploited vulnerability
no later than 14 days after a corrective or mitigating measure is available
within one month after the submission of the incident notification under point (b)
Article 14 shall apply from 11 September 2026
This Regulation shall apply from 11 December 2027.
an early warning notification of an actively exploited vulnerability, without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours of the manufacturer becoming aware of it

an early warning notification of a severe incident having an impact on the security of the product with digital elements, without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours of the manufacturer becoming aware of it
within 72 hours of the manufacturer becoming aware of the incident
CNAs MUST develop, document, and operate within a Scope Definition
the Scope Definition MUST include a covered set of Products and MUST NOT only list non-covered items.
Conditions or behaviors that do not lead to a security impact SHOULD NOT be determined to be Vulnerabilities.
CNAs SHOULD consider whether the Vulnerabilities are Independently Fixable.
The CNA with the most appropriate scope MUST be contacted and given the first opportunity to assign.
CNAs SHOULD assign different CVE IDs to different, Independently Fixable Vulnerabilities.
If a CNA is uncertain whether two issues are Independently Fixable, then the CNA SHOULD assign a single CVE ID.
Version: 4.2.6
Effective date: 2026-October-20
CNAs MUST develop, document, and operate within a Scope Definition
For Scope Definitions based on Products, the Scope Definition MUST include a covered set of Products and MUST NOT only list non-covered items.
Conditions or behaviors that do not lead to a security impact SHOULD NOT be determined to be Vulnerabilities.
CNAs SHOULD consider whether the Vulnerabilities are Independently Fixable.
The CNA with the most appropriate scope MUST be contacted and given the first opportunity to assign.
CNAs MUST assign different CVE IDs to different, Independently Fixable Vulnerabilities.
If a CNA is uncertain whether two issues are Independently Fixable, then the CNA SHOULD assign a single CVE ID.
A CNA MUST provide a method to request and coordinate CVE ID assignment
